subject: Clarify default retention for PII in request logs + EU delete workflow
messages:
From: Sara Liu <sara.liu@brightbank.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
Cc: security@brightbank.com
Date: Mon, 20 May 2029 15:12:00 +0100
Subject: Questions on data retention defaults - PII in requests

Hi Ava,

Thanks for taking this. Our security team has a few specific clarifications before we can sign off on the pilot: which categories of data are kept by default in hosted requests/responses (we're primarily worried about PII in prompts), and separately, what the default retention window is for those items? The questionnaire we attached has a couple of example flows (search, redaction, human review).

Two concrete asks:
- Can you confirm whether "prompts" (user inputs) are stored by default for hosted customers, and if so for how long?
- For generated outputs (the model's text), are those stored by default or only stored when a customer enables storage for evaluation?

We've attached our security questionnaire (BrightBank_Security_Questions.pdf). If you can point us to the exact wording we can provide to our Risk team (and to any contract addendum about EU residency), that'd be ideal.

Best,
Sara
Senior InfoSec Manager, BrightBank

Attachment: BrightBank_Security_Questions.pdf

From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@brightbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 May 2029 16:05:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Questions on data retention defaults - PII in requests

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear list. Quick summary up front, then Marissa/Karthik will add policy specifics and deletion-runbook pointers:

Summary (high level)
- Prompts (user-submitted text) are treated as part of the request payload and are retained by default for hosted customers; default window: 60 days.
- Request/response telemetry (status, latencies, minimal metadata) is retained 90 days by default for internal operational analytics.
- Generated outputs are not retained by default for long-term storage; by default outputs are transient and not indexed/persisted beyond short-term processing unless the customer opts into retention for evaluation or logging.

Sara — two quick questions before Marissa replies: do you need proof-of-deletion artifacts (audit records / hashes) or a contractual SLA that the purge completes within X days? Also, are you planning to use our hosted EU region or a Private (VPC) deployment? That changes residency options.

I'll leave details to Marissa for the exact policy language we can share.

— Ava
Product Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>, Sara Liu <sara.liu@brightbank.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 May 2029 17:40:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Questions on data retention defaults - PII in requests

Hi Sara,

Thanks for the attachment — reviewed quickly. Below is the precise policy language you can paste into your questionnaire, plus examples and the EU-specific options.

Policy excerpts (paste-ready)
1) Default capture and retention (hosted):
- Request payloads (user prompts and any attached metadata provided in the call) are captured by default and retained for 60 days. Retention exists to support debugging, abuse detection, and quality regressions.
- Model-generated outputs are treated as transient by default: we do not persist generated text to long-term storage, except where customers explicitly enable "retention for evaluation". When retention for evaluation is enabled by the customer, outputs are retained for the configured period (customer-controlled).
- Service telemetry (metrics, error traces, sampling of logs) is retained for 90 days by default for operational analytics. This telemetry does not include full request payloads unless sampling is configured.

2) EU residency and contractual controls:
- Customers requiring EU residency can be provisioned on our EU-hosted control plane and compute clusters; in that configuration, both capture and any retained artifacts remain within EU regions by default.
- For customers needing shorter retention (e.g., BrightBank's "30-day" requirement), we support a per-account retention configuration for request payloads and telemetry at the account level; reduction to 30 days is configurable and can be enforced via an addendum to the subscription agreement.

3) Deletion workflow and proof artifacts:
- Deletion request path: upon request, we mark targeted artifacts as tombstoned; tombstoned data is removed from live query surfaces immediately and queued for permanent purge.
- Purge timeline (hosted): permanent purge completes within 7 calendar days after tombstone for standard hosted accounts; for EU-hosted accounts the same timeline applies unless otherwise contracted.
- Proof of deletion: we can provide a deletion certificate (timestamped record with object identifiers and purge completion time) for compliance reviews. For extremely sensitive cases, we can provide a hashed digest and signing certificate for the purge run.

Examples (copy to questionnaire)
- Q: Do you store prompts? A: By default prompts in request payloads are stored for 60 days in hosted environments; customers can request a reduced window (e.g., 30 days) via contract for EU-hosted accounts.
- Q: Are outputs stored? A: No — outputs are transient unless the customer explicitly toggles retention for evaluation; if enabled, the retention period is customer-configurable.

Operational notes
- If BrightBank needs immediate purge on contract signature, we can include a clause to auto-set retention to 30 days from day 1 and run an initial purge for any pre-existing artifacts.
- For Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments, the default is that Redwood does not retain custody of data; retention rules are applied by BrightBank via our configuration tool.

Related runbook and evidence
- Runbook: https://redwood-internal.company/retention-runbook
- We can share SOC 2 artifact snippets and a redacted deletion certificate on request (we will coordinate through Security Ops).

—Marissa
Director, Product Security | Redwood Inference

From: Sara Liu <sara.liu@brightbank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 May 2029 08:23:00 +0100

Marissa — thank you, this is helpful and close to what our Risk team needs. Two follow-ups:
1) For the "tombstone -> purge in 7 days" flow, can you confirm the deletion certificate includes the object IDs and a signed timestamp?
2) If we contractually set account-level retention to 30 days, do you perform an initial backfill purge to bring historical artifacts within the new window, and if so how long does that backfill purge take?

We prefer the EU-hosted environment; contract team will request the addendum.

Sara

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@brightbank.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 May 2029 18:45:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Questions on data retention defaults - PII in requests

Hi Sara — quick answers to your two follow-ups: 

1) Deletion certificate: yes. Certificate contents: list of object identifiers (internal retention IDs), tombstone timestamp, purge completion timestamp, and a signed SHA256 digest of the purge job output. We can redact internal-only fields for customer-facing copies but will always include the object identifiers and signed timestamps.

2) Initial backfill purge: when an account-level retention change is applied we run a single backfill that identifies artifacts older than the new window and schedules them for purge; typical completion time for BrightBank-scale accounts is 24–72 hours depending on volume. We prioritize EU-hosted purges to remain entirely within EU data centers. If you need a contractual SLA for completion time we can include a 72-hour purge SLA in the addendum.

Next steps: Ava — I'll prepare a short paste-ready block to include in the security questionnaire and open a HubSpot ticket to track the addendum request. Sara — I'll loop Legal after we confirm the SLA and the specific EU region.

Regards,
Karthik
VP, Product | Redwood Inference
